routes.description: Establish classical theism by reasoning from the present dependence, contingency, and actualization of created things to a necessary sustaining source, then defend the coherence and goodness of that source against objections from freedom, temporal knowledge, evil, and hiddenness.
routes.successCriteria: The route succeeds if vertical causal dependence requires a necessary and purely actual divine ground, the relevant divine attributes remain mutually coherent, and suffering, nonbelief, and religious diversity are compatible with providential goodness and revelation.

motionBridge.description: Show that the necessary explanatory source reached through Thomistic metaphysics possesses the attributes required for the God of classical theism and remains credible after the principal objections.

centralBridges.description: Establish that contingent beings and act-potency causal series require a concurrent sustaining cause rather than merely an earliest temporal cause.
Connect the sustaining explanatory source to pure actuality and the divine attributes characteristic of classical theism.
Explain how pure actuality permits divine freedom and how eternal causal knowledge encompasses temporal change without change in God.
Reconcile divine goodness and providence with creaturely evil, suffering, hiddenness, and diverse forms of religious access.

subsidiaryBridges.description: Explain why knowledge of God can be naturally accessible while remaining difficult enough to warrant revelation and unequal human uptake.
Supply the teleological and analogical framework needed to predicate goodness of God and evaluate created suffering within an ordered whole.

routes.description: Undermine classical theism by challenging the inferences from dependent causal series to one purely actual, good, worship-worthy God and by arguing that pure actuality conflicts with divine freedom and changing knowledge while evolutionary suffering and nonresistant nonbelief count against perfect providential love.
routes.successCriteria: The route succeeds if the Thomistic causal arguments leave material explanatory or identification gaps, classical divine attributes generate unresolved contradictions, or the observed patterns of suffering and nonbelief are sufficiently unexpected under a perfectly good and loving God.

motionBridge.description: Show that the proposed classical God is not established by the Thomistic arguments and is independently undermined by conceptual and evidential objections.

centralBridges.description: Challenge concurrent conservation, termination, common-cause, pure-actuality, perfect-goodness, and worship-worthiness steps in the Thomistic inference.
Argue that a purely actual and immutable God cannot possess alternative-possibility freedom or knowledge responsive to a changing temporal world.
Establish that extensive apparently gratuitous animal suffering is improbable under perfect providential goodness and remains morally assessable.
Argue that nonresistant unbelief and persistent incompatible religious traditions conflict with the expectations generated by perfect divine love.

subsidiaryBridges.description: Ground objective judgments about needless suffering in irreducible normative truths without requiring natural teleology or a divine creator.
Present existential inertia as a coherent alternative to the claim that creatures require continuous divine conservation.

sections.title: Causal Dependence, Conservation, and Identification of God
sections.rationale: This issue contains the affirmative route from contingent, actualized beings to a sustaining necessary cause and the objections concerning existential inertia, infinite or multiple termini, pure actuality, goodness, and worship-worthiness.

sections.title: Pure Actuality and Divine Freedom
sections.rationale: The compatibility of pure actuality with free creation is a distinct burden because classical theism must explain how divine action is internally principled and genuinely free without unrealized potentialities or alternative possibilities.

sections.title: Immutability, Eternity, and Knowledge of Temporal Change
sections.rationale: This section tests whether eternal causal knowledge can encompass changing temporal truths without acquisition or loss in God, including challenges arising across competing theories of time.

sections.title: Evolutionary Evil, Divine Goodness, and Providence
sections.rationale: The scale and apparent gratuitousness of animal and human suffering directly bear on perfect goodness, while the opposing framework invokes transcendence, privation, creaturely freedom, redemptive goods, teleology, and cosmic order.

sections.title: Divine Hiddenness, Revelation, and Religious Diversity
sections.rationale: This issue joins claims about natural accessibility and accommodated revelation with objections from nonresistant nonbelief and religious disagreement, testing what epistemic access a perfectly loving God would provide.

chunk-001:c002.proposition: God's existence is accessible to natural reason yet also revealed because rational discovery is difficult, error-prone, and not immediately obvious.

chunk-001:c006.proposition: Causal chains in which potencies become actual cannot actualize themselves and require an actuality capable of grounding their interdependent causal relations.

chunk-002:chunk-002-candidate-03.proposition: God's eternal causal knowledge does not change with temporal creatures because the divine plan accounts for every creaturely change without itself undergoing change.

chunk-002:chunk-002-candidate-04.proposition: Divine freedom consists in action from an interior intellectual principle rather than the availability of alternatives, so pure actuality and a fixed end do not eliminate freedom.

chunk-002:chunk-002-candidate-10.proposition: The evolutionary-evil objection misclassifies God as one cause among others, whereas the transcendent creator produces both actuality and the conditions in which potentiality and defect are possible.

chunk-004:c004-03.proposition: A creature made from nothing lacks an underlying material source from which to subsist independently, so its act of being must remain imparted by God.

chunk-004:c004-10.proposition: Whether suffering is gratuitous must be judged relative to creatures' ends and the world's ordered harmony, whose ultimate purpose is manifesting God's glory rather than serving each creature's particular needs.

chunk-005:c005-07.proposition: Divine hiddenness is compatible with love because gradual, dramatic, and non-overwhelming revelation suits embodied rational creatures and preserves a freely developing relationship with God.

chunk-001:c009.proposition: Evolution's immense, inefficient, and frequently biologically or morally useless suffering is significant evidence against a perfectly good providential creator.

chunk-002:chunk-002-candidate-01.proposition: A purely actual God lacks potentialities and contingencies, cannot have done otherwise, and therefore cannot possess the perfect freedom affirmed by traditional theism.

chunk-002:chunk-002-candidate-02.proposition: Real temporal change requires God's knowledge to acquire and lose truths, contradicting the immutability and absence of potency asserted by classical theism.

chunk-002:chunk-002-candidate-05.proposition: Perfect divine love would keep every finite person able to enter a loving relationship with God, making nonresistant unbelief evidence against perfect divine goodness.

chunk-002:chunk-002-candidate-06.proposition: The first three Thomistic ways commit a quantifier-shift error because each causal chain having a first cause does not entail one shared first cause of every chain.

chunk-002:chunk-002-candidate-08.proposition: The Thomistic causal arguments do not establish a perfectly good or worship-worthy being, so further argument is required to bridge from a first cause to God.

chunk-004:c004-02.proposition: The changing-knowledge argument does not require presentism because propositions vary in truth across temporal locations even under eternalism or growing-block theories.

chunk-004:c004-07.proposition: Soul-building and redemptive accounts do not answer evolutionary evil because nonhuman animals endured immense gratuitous pain and little flourishing before moral agents existed.

chunk-005:c005-04.proposition: Widespread incompatible religious traditions are surprising if a perfectly loving God exists, making religious disagreement a stronger objection than surface parallels among religions.
